clues: This small town sits at the far inner end of the Bay of Kotor. Narrow straits link it out to the open sea.
The steep plateau above town gets more rain than any place in Europe. Over 5000 mm falls there each year, a European record.
This place began in ancient times as the first town on its bay. No other town on the bay is as old.
Strong springs rise near the shore here. They join to form a short brook through a thin belt of green farmland.
Look for the tall pale cliffs of the highest range on this coast of the Adriatic Sea. They guard the town from the land behind it.
